answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer: No, there is not time for a 22, and you do not need one. You already ran 20 miles on Sep 13 and 17 miles last Sunday with a tiny heart-rate drift, which is the fitness signal we wanted. Another step up now would cost more than it gives: recovery eats into the taper, and the last long run before race day should leave your legs fresh, not wrung out. The playbook from here is one more medium-long with marathon pace in it this Sunday, then two progressively lighter weeks. Trust the 20 you banked.

new.analysis:
You executed last week cleanly: five runs, 42 miles, every session matched the plan, and the long run drifted less than 5 bpm. That is the profile of someone ready to race, not someone short of work.

The job now flips from building to sharpening. This week keeps the structure you know, with one marathon-pace session midweek and a shorter long run that finishes at target pace. The point is to rehearse 8:35/mi feeling under control, not to chase more miles.

Your target of 3:45 works out to 8:35/mi, so use that number on Wednesday and the last 4 miles Sunday. If heart rate climbs above 165 while you are on pace, ease back rather than push; the race will reward patience far more than one hero workout. Next week I will take the long run down to around 11 or 12, and race week will be very light.

On the anxiety: the fitness has not changed because the calendar did. Keep sleep, food and routines boring over the next 20 days and let the training speak on the day.
